spec.description: Novice SOC Hub - Bird's eye view

spec.title: 🩺 How is the system doing?
spec.description: Section header. The six tiles below it are simple up/down health checks for each subsystem Home-IDS depends on — Pi-hole, Zeek, the ML model, the router integration, and the Layer-2 tarpit. Green = running normally. Red = that subsystem is down and the protection it provides is currently NOT active.

options.content:
**Are my shields online?**

These panels show if the underlying security engines are currently running and protecting you.

spec.title: Total Active Isolations
spec.description: How many devices are RIGHT NOW under active hardware containment (Layer-2 ARP tarpit and/or Layer-3 router isolation combined). 0 is the normal, healthy state. Any non-zero value means a device is currently isolated — check the Master Threat Ledger below to see which one and why.

spec.title: 📜 High-Priority Security Alerts (Live Timeline)
spec.description: A live, scrolling feed of every alert the engine has classified as verdict = CONFIRMED_THREAT (i.e. NOT suppressed by the false-positive engine). This is your primary 'what just happened' feed. Each row is one evaluated alert with its full evidence JSON. Sourced from alerts.json via Loki job="home_ids_alerts".

spec.title: Lifetime Threats Blocked
spec.description: Lifetime running total of domains Pi-hole has sinkholed on Home-IDS's instruction (Layer 7 / DNS containment, metric home_ids_ips_pihole_blocks_aggregate_total). This mitigation layer fires immediately and autonomously the moment a threat is confirmed, regardless of the interactive_blocking_enabled setting — DNS blocking is never gated behind Telegram approval. See the new 'Pi-hole Sinkhole Rate' panel further down for the trend.

spec.title: Total Alerts Triaged
spec.description: Lifetime count of alerts that crossed detection_engine.alert_threshold (6.0) and were sent through the full evaluation pipeline, whether they ended up confirmed or suppressed as false positives.

spec.title: Pi-hole IPS
spec.description: Is the Pi-hole DNS sinkhole integration currently reachable and authenticated? Green = Home-IDS can issue blocklist commands to Pi-hole right now. Red = Layer 7 (DNS) containment is not functioning — check pihole_integration config and the PIHOLE_API_PASSWORD / PIHOLE_API_URL secrets in .env.

spec.title: Zeek Network Monitor
spec.description: Is Zeek's log stream currently being read? Green = the engine is actively tailing conn.log/dns.log and extracting network features. Red = Brain 1 has lost its primary sensor and is flying blind on network-level detections (port scans, JA3/JA4 fingerprints, lateral movement).

spec.title: AI Model Loaded
spec.description: Has the global scikit-learn IsolationForest baseline model (models/ids_model.pkl) loaded successfully? Green = new/unknown devices get a working anomaly baseline. Red = anomaly scoring for devices that haven't hit their own ml_warmup_samples yet is effectively disabled.

spec.title: Router Kill-Switch
spec.description: Is the Fritz!Box TR-064 router integration configured and reachable? This gates Layer-3 hardware isolation (severing a device's WAN access). Red doesn't mean you're unprotected — Layer 7 (Pi-hole) and Layer 2 (ARP tarpit) still work independently — it just means the router 'kill switch' specifically is unavailable.

spec.title: Layer-2 Tarpit
spec.description: Is the Layer-2 Scapy ARP/NDP tarpit subsystem armed and ready? This is usually the fastest-acting containment layer since it works purely on the local LAN with no external API dependency. Red here is worth investigating first if a device seems to stay online despite being 'isolated'.

spec.title: API Integrations
spec.description: Minimum status across ALL configured external integrations (Pi-hole, router, and — depending on your build — threat-intel APIs). Shows red if even ONE integration you've enabled is currently failing, so you don't have to check every tile individually.

spec.title: Alert Queue
spec.description: How many evaluated alerts are currently sitting in the processing queue waiting for Brain 2 (CL-AFPE) to decide suppress-vs-confirm. Should hover near 0 in normal operation. A sustained climb usually means the false-positive engine or an external threat-intel lookup is stalling — check LGBM Model Status and API Integrations above.

spec.title: 📖 How to read the Master Ledger
spec.description: Section header for the Master Threat Ledger below — explains how to read it.

options.content:
**The bird's-eye view of your entire home.**

Each row is a device. The columns are different AI and heuristic checks. If a column turns **red**, that device is acting suspiciously in that specific way.

spec.title: 🛡️ What did the system block for me?
spec.description: Section header for the three lifetime counters to the right — explains that they answer 'how many threats has this thing actually stopped for me'.

options.content: Check the counters below to see how many threats were neutralized today.

spec.title: 🚨 Master Threat Ledger (Complete Multi-Vector Device Matrix)
spec.description: The single most important panel in this dashboard set. One row per device, one column per detection signal — statistical (Threat Confidence, ML Outlier, Markov Score, Risk Velocity), threat-intel (TI Risk, AbuseIPDB, VirusTotal), network (JA4+ Hits, Honeypot, Lateral Moves, DoH Intercepts, Port Scans, Outbound Bytes, TXT/NULL Abuse), and containment/lifecycle state (Fritz! Router Block, Layer-2 Tarpit Trapped, Kill-Chain Phase, Probation, Baseline Frozen, Safe Listed). Sort by Threat Confidence to triage fastest. Click a hostname to open its full Device Deep Dive page. Thresholds on the Threat Confidence column (🟢 0-3.99 / 🟡 4-5.99 / 🟠 6-7.99 / 🔴 8+) mirror the engine's own detection_engine.alert_threshold = 6.0 — anything 🟠 or worse has already crossed the line that triggers a real alert.

spec.title: 🧭 New Here? Start With This
spec.description: A guided orientation for first-time operators: what the 4 dashboards are for, what the color thresholds mean, and what to actually do when a device turns red.

options.content:
### Welcome — start here

This is one of **4 linked dashboards**. Use the links at the top-right of every dashboard (or the corner **Navigation** menu) to jump between them:

1. **Overview** (this page) — is the system healthy, and what's the current threat picture across your whole network?
2. **Threat Landscape** — where is the threat coming from (countries, C2, DNS tunneling, scanning)?
3. **Device Deep Dive** — pick one device and see its full history.
4. **System Tuning, Healing & Health** — how the AI is tuning itself, what it's silently suppressed, and whether the engine process itself is healthy.

**What the colors mean everywhere in this dashboard set:** 🟢 Safe (0-3.99) → 🟡 Monitoring (4-5.99) → 🟠 Suspicious (6-7.99, this is the engine's real alert_threshold) → 🔴 Critical (8+). These bands are not arbitrary — they come directly from `detection_engine.alert_threshold: 6.0` in `config.yaml`.

**If you see a 🔴 Critical device:** open its row link to go to Device Deep Dive, read the Kill-Chain Phase and which specific signals fired (TI/AbuseIPDB/VirusTotal flags = reputation, Port Scans/Lateral Moves = it's attacking other devices, Outbound Bytes spike = possible data exfiltration). If `interactive_blocking_enabled` is on, you'll get a Telegram prompt to approve isolation; DNS sinkholing (Pi-hole) has already happened automatically regardless. Use the Isolate/Release links on the Hostname column to act immediately without waiting for Telegram.

spec.title: 📈 Alerts Triaged Over Time
spec.description: Trend view of home_ids_alerts_total (same counter as the 'Total Alerts Triaged' tile above, shown as a rate so you can see whether alert volume is rising, falling, or spiking — a sudden spike is worth investigating even if each individual alert looks minor).

spec.title: 🚫 Pi-hole Sinkhole Rate (Blocks / min)
spec.description: How fast Home-IDS is instructing Pi-hole to sinkhole domains, derived from the same home_ids_ips_pihole_blocks_aggregate_total counter as the 'Lifetime Threats Blocked' tile above. This is Layer 7 containment — it fires immediately and autonomously, independent of interactive_blocking_enabled. A sustained non-zero rate means active threats are being neutralized at the DNS level right now.
